correctness.rationale: Conditioning on target R fixed across resets yields a renewal ratio, with erf survival and an exact antiderivative. The rational interval verifier uses proved Taylor remainder enclosures and Machin pi bounds to show the mixed two-atom clock is <4.2; its three analytic/interval regimes cover every deterministic duration with bounds >4.25; positive Bernstein coefficients plus a monotone tail certify the >4.25 bound for every exponential clock. Single-target minimality follows from exact positive ratio weights, with no finite simulation substituted for the infinite-range comparisons.

value.rationale: Persistent target uncertainty is a natural physical modification of the classical restart problem. The result resolves the smallest possible number of target locations needed to defeat sharp-clock optimality: one is impossible and two are sufficient, even under bounded target uncertainty. Exact bounds for two ubiquitous comparator protocol families give substantive nonlocal optimization information, rather than an arbitrary isolated statistic.
